choices: The number of hours since lights-on before the next irrigation event.
The reduction in root-zone water content between irrigation events or defined comparison points.
The amount of nutrient concentrate added during fertigation.
Any event in which runoff is observed from the container.
rationale: Dryback refers to the decrease in root-zone water content over time, typically between irrigation events or other defined points. It is not simply elapsed time, nutrient amount, or runoff occurrence. Keeping that definition clear prevents the technician from confusing a moisture trend with an irrigation event or recipe variable.
